sentences.text: Tanycolagreus was a coelurosaurian theropod dinosaur that lived approximately 152 million years ago during the Late Jurassic in North America.
The holotype specimen represents a subadult individual measuring about 3.3 meters, though other fossils suggest adults could reach 4 meters.
This predator featured a large, elongated head with a blunt snout and possessed long legs that were lightly built.
The name means 'long-limbed hunter' because its forelimbs and hindlimbs are longer than those of Coelurus.
The species name topwilsoni honors George Eugene 'Top' Wilson, the father of a benefactor who supported the research.
A partial skeleton was found in 1995 at the Bone Cabin Quarry West locality in Wyoming before being donated to science by an anonymous benefactor.
Although initially thought to be Coelurus, it was formally named and described by Kenneth Carpenter, Clifford Miles, and Karen Cloward in 2005.
The holotype includes an incomplete skull, lower jaws, and much of the body skeleton behind the head, while the skull remains less well known than the postcranial skeleton.
The second toe was slightly hyperextendable but lacked an enlarged claw.
In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated that a four-meter-long Tanycolagreus would weigh approximately 120 kilograms.
A 2007 phylogenetic analysis placed Tanycolagreus in a basal position within the Tyrannosauroidea.
Later analyses suggested that Tanycolagreus held a basal position within the Coelurosauria.
Carpenter and colleagues originally assigned Tanycolagreus to the family Coeluridae, but it belongs to the parent group Coelurosauria.
Fossils of Tanycolagreus come from the Morrison Formation, dated to the Oxfordian to Tithonian stages, and are present in stratigraphic zone 2.
It is debated whether Tanycolagreus belongs to the Proceratosauridae; some 2025 analyses tentatively include it there, while others place it near but outside that family.
